title: Neonatal Jaundice (AAP 2022)
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: Neonatal Jaundice
Kemper AR et al. AAP Clinical Practice Guideline Revision: management of hyperbilirubinemia in the newborn ≥ 35 weeks. Pediatrics 2022;150(3):e2022058859

changelog.change: Initial entry — AAP 2022 revision: raised (risk-stratified) phototherapy thresholds, universal screening, the 'escalation of care' concept, and the physiologic-vs-pathologic + conjugated-vs-unconjugated framework.

purpose: The AAP 2022 guideline raised phototherapy thresholds modestly and made screening universal. Use the current GA- and risk-stratified TSB nomograms, not a single flat number — the old 'rarely > 12 mg/dL is fine' heuristic predates this update.

items: Universal TSB or transcutaneous bilirubin (TcB) at 24–48 h of life, or before discharge if sooner, in every infant ≥ 35 wk GA.
Jaundice before 24 h of age is ALWAYS pathologic — urgent evaluation.

Any elevated DIRECT (conjugated) bilirubin (> 1 mg/dL) is always pathologic — evaluate for liver injury (TORCH, sepsis, galactosemia, α1-antitrypsin) or obstruction (biliary atresia — time-critical for Kasai; choledochal cyst).
Pathologic unconjugated pattern: onset day 1, rate of rise > 5 mg/dL/day or > 0.5 mg/dL/hr, associated anemia / hepatosplenomegaly / sepsis signs, or persistence beyond 1–2 weeks.

body.text: Escalation of care — evaluate urgently if

Onset < 24 h · TSB approaching or exceeding the phototherapy threshold for the GA / risk category · rate of rise > 0.5 mg/dL/hr · any sign of acute bilirubin encephalopathy (lethargy, poor feeding, high-pitched cry, arching / opisthotonos) · jaundice beyond 2–3 weeks with dark urine or pale stool (conjugated / obstructive — biliary atresia). Use the current AAP 2022 GA- and risk-factor-stratified TSB graphs for both phototherapy initiation and the escalation decision — not a fixed number.

rows: Lactation support, increase feeding frequency; supplement only if medically indicated
Usually observation. If diagnostic uncertainty, a brief 24–48 h interruption with pumping shows a rapid bilirubin drop. Rarely needs phototherapy.

items: Phototherapy: infant undressed, eyes and gonads shielded, light source per device instructions, turn periodically, monitor temperature and hydration. Start per the AAP 2022 GA/risk threshold graph.
Exchange transfusion (double-volume, via umbilical vessels): reserved for TSB reaching the higher exchange threshold, or any sign of acute bilirubin encephalopathy.
IVIG: consider in isoimmune haemolytic disease (Rh / ABO) if TSB keeps rising despite intensive phototherapy — reduces the need for exchange transfusion.

body.text: Kernicterus = deposition of unbound unconjugated bilirubin in the basal ganglia and brainstem. Acute bilirubin encephalopathy progresses: lethargy / poor feeding / hypotonia → irritability / hypertonia / opisthotonos / fever → opisthotonos, apnoea, coma. Chronic sequelae: choreoathetoid CP, upward-gaze palsy, sensorineural hearing loss, dental enamel dysplasia. Timely screening and treatment prevents it; established encephalopathy is hard to treat.

buildNote: Tier 1 (currency — AAP 2022, valid through Aug 2027). The actual hour-specific Bhutani nomogram and the GA/risk threshold graphs are media the app still needs; this module carries the decision logic and the escalation triggers.
